headerDisplay: Watches the power draw of Matter smart plugs and power meters, such as the Eve Energy or the Shelly Plug PM Gen3, and shows each appliance in HomeKit with a Running switch that turns off when it is done. It learns each appliance's thresholds from its first cycle. Run it as a child bridge.
footerDisplay: The plugs stay in Apple Home: this plugin joins them as a second controller (Matter multi-admin). For devices on Thread, the Raspberry Pi needs a route to the Thread network — on Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm it has one already; the README says how to check.

name.title: Name
name.description: Used for the sensors, in the log and in the recording. A paired plug is remembered by this name, so renaming it means pairing it again.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: On its dashboard tile, in the Home look.

pairingCode.title: Pairing code
pairingCode.description: In the Home app: the plug's settings → Turn On Pairing Mode. The code is valid for 15 minutes, so save and restart the child bridge straight away. Only needed once; it can be removed after pairing.

pairedWith.title: Shares the pairing of
pairedWith.description: For a device behind a Matter bridge: the name of the appliance that paired the bridge. A bridge is paired once; the devices behind it share that pairing, each choosing one device below.

deviceId.title: Device behind the bridge
deviceId.description: Which device of a bridge this appliance follows: the bridged device's UniqueID, which the log lists after connecting. Empty: every reading of the plug counts.

partOf.title: Part of
partOf.description: The name of another appliance whose plug also measures this one: a lamp that reports its own watts, plugged into a metered socket strip, say. It keeps its own figures but stays out of every total, so it is not counted twice, and draws nothing while that appliance is switched off or draws nothing.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: The same by endpoint number, for a device without UniqueID — a channel of a plug with several, say.

runningSwitch.title: Running switch
runningSwitch.description: A switch that is on while the appliance runs, to hang automations on: when it turns off, the appliance is done. Named after the appliance, followed by Running; rename it in the Home app.

runningAs.title: Show Running as
runningAs.description: An occupancy sensor reads better for a desk: taken while it draws power, free when not. An outlet only looks like one: tapping it switches nothing. Changing it replaces it in HomeKit, with any automation on it.

overtimeMinutes.title: Overtime after (minutes)
overtimeMinutes.description: Sensor on after running this long in one go. Empty: none.

idleOnMinutes.title: Idle after (minutes)
idleOnMinutes.description: Sensor on after drawing power this long without running, or this long after the end of the phase below. Empty: none.

idleOnFrom.title: Idle counted from (phase)
idleOnFrom.description: Count Idle from the end of this phase instead. Empty: from when it stops running.

pollSeconds.title: Polling interval (seconds)
pollSeconds.description: Some plugs report their power only about once a minute (the Eve Energy does), which can miss something short like a coffee. Set this to ask them more often. Each ask is a message over the network, so keep it to the plugs that need it. A plug that draws nothing is not asked.

thresholds.title: Fixed thresholds
thresholds.description: Optional. Leave a field empty to have it learned from the appliance's cycles; fill it in to use your value instead.

startSeconds.title: Running: for at least (seconds above, added up)

finishSeconds.title: Finished: quiet for (seconds below the running power)

phases.title: Phases
phases.description: What the appliance does inside a cycle, told apart by power: heating, spinning, a coffee running through. Easiest to add from the Power tab, by picking a level or a stretch of time on the recorded curve.

name.title: Name
name.description: Also the name of its switch in HomeKit; rename it in the Home app.

maxWatts.title: Below (W)
maxWatts.description: Leave empty for "from and up", as for heating.

minSeconds.title: On after (seconds in the range, added up)

holdSeconds.title: Off after (seconds out of the range)

maxSeconds.title: Only if shorter than (seconds in the range)
maxSeconds.description: Only draws shorter than this are the phase. Since that is known only once the draw is over, the switch then goes on for a moment, like Finished. A rinse beside a coffee: the same range, the coffee on after 10 s, the rinse shorter than 10 s.

onDown.title: On down
onDown.description: Only when the draw falls into the range from above, not when it rises into it. A washing machine that has finished rests at the same few watts as one just switched on to be loaded.

sensor.title: Switch in HomeKit
sensor.description: A switch that is on while the phase lasts, named after the phase.

count.title: Count in statistics
count.description: Show how often this phase happened on the Statistics tab, instead of the finished cycles. If more than one phase is ticked, the first one counts.

recordPower.title: Record power readings
recordPower.description: Write every reading to a file per day under appliance-monitor/power in the Homebridge storage folder. The Power tab needs it.

recordDays.title: Days of recordings to keep
recordDays.description: One file per day under appliance-monitor/power, for the Power tab. The statistics keep their own daily totals for two years and do not need these files.

matterLogLevel.title: matter.js log level
matterLogLevel.description: How much of the Matter library's own logging to show. Info and debug appear only with Homebridge debug logging on.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: A read-only web page with each appliance's power now, its chart and the statistics, at http://<this machine>:<port>/. No login: anyone on the network can see it, nobody can change anything.

dashboardPort.title: Dashboard port
dashboardPort.description: The port of the dashboard; 8582 if empty.
